name: eve_industry_calculator
summary: Calculator for EVE Online industry that explodes T2/PI/reaction recipes down to base materials, with hangar-aware netting.
description:
Helps calculate what materials are needed to produce advanced items in EVE Online (mainly Tech 2 items, but also covers the PI and moon-goo reaction chains that feed into them). T2 blueprints require many different material types across several tiers: base minerals (e.g. Tritanium, Morphite) are used directly in single-step manufacturing (e.g. Acolyte I drones, R.A.M. Robotics); Planetary Industry products form a P1 -> P2 -> P3 chain (each P2 made from 2 P1 basic materials, each P3 made from 2-3 P2 products, e.g. Robotics <- Consumer Electronics + Mechanical Parts); and moon-goo reaction chains produce things like Laser Focusing Crystals through their own multi-step batch reactions (e.g. Tungsten Carbide batches of 10000 <- Sulfuric Acid + Rolled Tungsten Alloy + Nitrogen Fuel Blocks, each of those built from further reactions). The app has three core use cases: (1) enter/edit recipes so they persist in the backend (recipes are mostly static reference data), (2) pick a recipe and a quantity to produce and get the fully recursive list of base materials required, first as a flat total and later as a step-by-step build plan showing what to craft at each tier, and (3) copy in the contents of your hangar so the calculator nets off materials/intermediates you already have at every tier (e.g. if you need 10 Robotics but have 4, it only asks for the Reactive Metals/Consumer Electronics needed for the remaining 6, and lets you reuse partially-built intermediates from earlier steps).

Architecture: 4 Docker containers - Angular frontend (recipe/item/category management UI, plus calculator pages that call backend calculation endpoints), PHP backend (owns persistence/API for recipes and hangar data, and now also BOM explosion/netting math - see key_decisions), MySQL database, and Adminer for DB inspection/administration. Deeper details (DB schema, API shape, recipe data model) are to be worked out when the relevant goals are tackled.

key_decisions.decision: 4-container Docker setup: Angular frontend, PHP backend, MySQL database, Adminer.
key_decisions.rationale: Keeps concerns separated and gives easy DB inspection via Adminer without building custom admin tooling.

key_decisions.decision: REVISED (2026-08-02, during 2_material_summary): BOM explosion and hangar-netting calculations move to the PHP backend, not the Angular frontend. The frontend calls an endpoint like "explode recipe 123 x30 runs" and gets back the resulting material breakdown, rather than holding the full recipe graph in memory and computing it client-side. The backend is no longer a purely dumb persistence layer - it now owns recipe-graph traversal too.
key_decisions.rationale: Original plan was a deliberately dumb backend that just serves all recipe/hangar data to the frontend for it to crunch. User decided against that: the frontend would need the entire recipe graph in memory to explode a BOM, whereas the backend already owns that graph relationally and can walk it directly (recursive query/PHP recursion) and return just the result. This also keeps 4_hangar_netting consistent, since netting logic sits on top of the same explosion and would otherwise have needed the reversal anyway.

key_decisions.decision: Exclude files/directories not relevant to the project itself via .gitignore - IDE metadata (e.g. PHPStorm's .idea/) and third-party libraries/dependency directories (e.g. vendor/, node_modules/).
key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the repository focused on project source; machine/user-specific and reproducible/installable files shouldn't be tracked.

key_decisions.decision: PHP backend uses Slim Framework (routing + PSR-7 request/response, JSON in/out) with PDO for MySQL persistence, rather than plain PHP or a full-stack framework like Symfony/Laravel.
key_decisions.rationale: User is familiar with Symfony but wanted something lighter for a pure JSON API with no bundles/DI container/scaffolding - fits the existing decision to keep the backend intentionally minimal.

key_decisions.decision: Source lives in two top-level directories: frontend/ (Angular app) and backend/ (PHP app), not nested under an apps/ folder.
key_decisions.rationale: Simple two-app monorepo layout; decided during docker_setup since both Dockerfiles and docker-compose.yml reference these paths directly.

key_decisions.decision: Docker commands (docker run, docker compose ...) must be prefixed with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 when run from Git Bash on Windows.
key_decisions.rationale: Git Bash rewrites POSIX-looking paths (e.g. /app used as a container path or working directory) into Windows paths before they reach Docker, causing errors like "the working directory 'C:/Program Files/Git/app' is invalid". This will recur on any future docker command run from this shell.

key_decisions.decision: DB schema migrations use robmorgan/phinx (backend/phinx.php config, migrations in backend/db/migrations/, applied via `php vendor/bin/phinx migrate -c phinx.php` from inside the backend container). The backend Docker image must be rebuilt (`docker compose build backend`) after adding/updating a composer dependency, since backend/vendor is an anonymous volume that only gets populated from the image on container creation - a plain `docker compose run` after editing composer.json will not see the new package.
key_decisions.rationale: User is used to Symfony/Doctrine migrations (PHP classes with up/down, able to run data-manipulation code, not just raw SQL) and wanted the closest equivalent without pulling in a full ORM - Phinx gives that on top of the already-minimal Slim+PDO backend. The rebuild-after-composer-change caveat was discovered when `vendor/bin/phinx` was 'not found' after a `composer require` run inside an ephemeral `docker compose run` container, because that container's anonymous vendor volume was destroyed on exit before the new package could be used.

key_decisions.decision: After any `backend/composer.json` change, rebuilding the image is not enough on its own once a persistent `backend` container has existed before - must also run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate --renew-anon-volumes backend` (not just `--force-recreate`).
key_decisions.rationale: Docker Compose preserves a service's anonymous volumes across container recreation by default (a deliberate anti-data-loss behavior, e.g. for accidentally-anonymous DB volumes), so a plain rebuild + restart silently keeps serving the stale pre-change `vendor/`. Discovered when the newly added `App\` PSR-4 autoload mapping (for task #5's RecipeTypes class) didn't take effect after a full `--no-cache` image rebuild, until `--renew-anon-volumes` was added. The plain-rebuild-is-enough note in the Phinx decision above only held up until backend-1 had been started once as a persistent (non `run --rm`) container - after that, this stronger form applies.

key_decisions.decision: Recipe data (item_categories/items/recipes/recipe_inputs) is persisted as a committed file, not trusted to the `mysql` Docker volume. `scripts/export-recipe-data.sh` dumps those tables to `backend/db/seeds/recipe_data.sql` on demand; a Phinx seed class (`RecipeDataSeeder`) truncates and re-imports from that file if it exists. `backend/docker-entrypoint.sh` runs `phinx migrate` then `phinx seed:run` automatically on every backend container start (with retry/backoff around migrate, since a first-time mysql volume init can briefly report healthy via a temporary bootstrap server before restarting into the real one, causing a connection-refused race).
key_decisions.rationale: User considers anything living only inside a Docker volume/container to be volatile - the real source of truth for recipe data must be a file that travels with the git repo, so copying the project to another machine (or wiping the volume) and running `docker compose up` reconstitutes schema + recipe data with zero manual DB steps.

key_decisions.decision: The Angular dev server proxies API calls itself: `frontend/proxy.conf.json` routes `/api/*` to `http://backend:8000` (stripping the `/api` prefix), wired via `angular.json`'s `serve.options.proxyConfig`. All frontend services call same-origin `/api/...` paths.
key_decisions.rationale: The backend has no CORS middleware; since the frontend is only ever run via `docker compose` (where it can reach the backend container by its service name), proxying at the dev server means the browser always talks same-origin to localhost:4200 and never needs CORS at all. Established while building 1_recipe_management's Recipe List page (task #9) and used by every frontend page since.

key_decisions.decision: EVE Online reaction recipes can have facility-bonus-adjusted material consumption per run that isn't an integer (e.g. Tungsten Carbide's base recipe is 100 Rolled Tungsten Alloy + 100 Sulfuric Acid -> 10000 output, but a bonused facility consumes 97.8 of each per run). For now these are entered as the rounded-up-to-integer per-run value (e.g. 98), since `recipe_inputs.input_quantity` is an integer column with no rounding-mode concept.
key_decisions.rationale: Rounding up per run is the safe direction (never runs short), and matches how the user actually plans production today. This is a known stopgap, not a permanent fix - it loses precision and doesn't scale correctly for a batch of N runs (round-up-per-run != round-up-once-for-N). Revisit when `2_material_summary`/`3_build_steps_breakdown` implement the actual BOM explosion math: either add float/decimal quantities with explicit rounding semantics, or store the base recipe and facility modifier separately.

key_decisions.decision: On Windows, invoking a `.sh` script directly (e.g. `bash ./scripts/export-recipe-data.sh`) from PowerShell, cmd, or a PHPStorm terminal can fail with a WSL relay error ("execvpe(/bin/bash) failed") because `bash` on PATH resolves to Windows' WSL launcher (`C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`), not Git Bash. Fix: call Git Bash's bash.exe explicitly, and in PowerShell use the call operator for a quoted exe path: `& "C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe" ./scripts/export-recipe-data.sh` (or an absolute forward-slash path like `D:/PHPStormProjects/eve_industry_calculator/scripts/...` to run from anywhere, since the script itself `cd`s to its own directory).
key_decisions.rationale: Discovered running `scripts/export-recipe-data.sh` during 2_material_summary. Will recur for any project shell script run outside a Git Bash window.
